Architecturally anchored on Estonia eGA twinning experience (EGA-KG-TWINNING is the active Estonia-Kyrgyzstan technical assistance vehicle). What is preserved: eGA's TOR drafting playbook for X-Road / Tunduk-class systems. What is adapted: KG-specific donor procurement rules, Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual deliverable requirements, and UDP's centralized governance structure.

short_name: Digital Som CBDC Wallet & AML/KYC Stack
one_liner: Deliver wallet, AML/KYC, fraud-detection and crypto-compliance AI stack for the digital som CBDC under NBKR ahead of mandatory 1 January 2027 go-live (Constitutional Law 74 of 16.04.2025).
problem_statement: KG-LAW-2025-074-NBKR-CBDC (16 April 2025) is a Constitutional Law amendment establishing the digital som with mandatory go-live on 1 January 2027. NBKR holds exclusive emission and platform-operation authority. Pilot is running through 2026. Live tender KG-T-2026-004 ($3.5M, digital som software infrastructure) is open and forthcoming KG-TF-2026-002 ($4.5M, Phase 2 offline transactions and AML/KYC) follows in 2026. Constitutional law deadlines cannot slip without legislative amendment — this is the rarest mandatory-by-law procurement event in Central Asia. Brazil Pix (case-br-pix), Singapore Project Ubin (case-sg-cbdc-project-ubin), and India UPI (case-in-upi) provide proven CBDC architecture blueprints.
solution_concept: Deliver a four-layer digital som platform stack: (1) consumer wallet (Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual, KYC-bound, MIR/SBP-interoperable for diaspora remittance corridor); (2) AML/KYC AI engine integrating NBKR sanctions lists and Tunduk identity fetch; (3) fraud-detection ML for transaction anomaly scoring at scale (target: 5M+ active wallets by 2028); (4) crypto-virtual-asset compliance layer cross-referencing the KGST stablecoin and the Virtual Assets Registry mandated by KG-LAW-2022-012-VIRTUAL and KG-LAW-2026-003-VA-AMEND. Architecturally anchored on Brazil Pix's centralized rail + Singapore Ubin's wholesale-to-retail bridge. Adapted for KG's hydropower-funded sovereign infrastructure preference and the labor migration remittance use case (Russia → KG corridor, $2.8B annually) where the digital som can capture 5–15% of transaction flow.
what_preserved: Brazil Pix architecture (centralized rail with rich open API surface, fraud detection via ML), Singapore Ubin wholesale-retail bridge pattern.
what_adapted: Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual UX, MIR/SBP remittance interoperability, Tunduk identity binding, NBKR sanctions list integration, virtual asset cross-compliance with KGST stablecoin registry.
regulatory_hurdles: Constitutional Law amendment status means infrastructure choices become semi-permanent. NBKR exclusive-emission rule blocks any non-NBKR custodial structure. Sanctions exposure on cross-border rails requires careful bank counterparty vetting. Mitigation: structure as software vendor to NBKR with no custodial role; design AML engine to flag and block any sanctioned-counterparty transaction at the rail level.
primary_funding: NBKR state budget + WB/IFC technical assistance + EFSD-KG-STABILIZATION digital infrastructure component
competitive_landscape: G+D, Giesecke+Devrient and IBM are global CBDC incumbents but have minimal Central Asia presence. Russian vendors (NSPK, Yandex) sanctions-exposed. Chinese vendors (Huawei) targeting infrastructure not application layer. Estonia eGA twinning includes fintech advisory but not CBDC stack delivery. The Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual + sntz.ai agentic stack + sanctions-clean positioning is differentiator. NBKR has run the pilot internally so operational know-how is on the buyer side; vendor differentiation is on speed, AML quality, and Russian-language coverage.

≥99.5% AML transaction screening latency < 200ms at pilot volume

Zero sanctioned-counterparty leakage in NBKR audit
Functional remittance corridor demo with at least one MIR/SBP-compatible test partner

Year 3 (2028): export the stack to NBKR's regional peers (Tajikistan, Mongolia exploring CBDC) and license the AML/fraud engine separately to commercial banks under KG-LAW-2024-121-CYBERSEC compliance frame.

one_liner: Modernize the Tunduk inter-agency data exchange platform (KG's X-Road equivalent) under live RFP KG-T-2026-005 ($1.8M) and the post-Минцифры transfer to UDP, replicating Estonia X-Road maturity gains.
problem_statement: Tunduk is the State Enterprise operating Kyrgyzstan's inter-agency data exchange platform (X-Road derivative). Following the Mintsifry liquidation, Tunduk SE was transferred to UDP control via KG-TUNDUK-INFOCOM-TRANSFER. Live RFP KG-T-2026-005 ($1.8M, Tunduk platform modernization — API gateway and data management) is open. KG-LAW-2025-178-DIGITAL-CODE and its enactment law (KG-LAW-2025-179-DIGITAL-CODE-ENACTMENT) require Tunduk to host the AI auditability and model registry mandated by the Digital Code. Existing platform is functional but lacks modern API gateway, observability, and the AI inference fabric needed for the next decade. Estonia X-Road / X-Tee (case-est-xroad) is the reference architecture; case-kg-tunduk-modernisation documents the ongoing modernization track.
solution_concept: Three-component delivery: (1) modern API gateway with OAuth2/OIDC, rate-limiting, circuit-breaker patterns and observability stack — replacing the current bespoke routing layer; (2) data-management plane with consent receipt management compliant with KG-LAW-2008-058 (personal information law) and Digital Code amendments; (3) AI inference fabric — a managed-runtime layer on which any government agency can deploy a model and have its consumption metered, logged for the Digital Code AI registry, and routed through Tunduk's identity layer. Architecturally anchored on Estonia X-Road maturity (case-est-xroad) preserved as core; adapted for KG's centralized UDP governance, Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual operator UX, and the Digital Code AI auditability requirements that are unique to KG.
what_preserved: X-Road peer-to-peer data exchange, message-level signing, audit trail, security server architecture — all production-proven across Estonia, Finland, Iceland.
what_adapted: Centralized UDP governance (KG model is more centralized than Estonia's distributed pattern), Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual operator console, AI registry and inference fabric layer (Digital Code requirement absent in Estonia), integration with the Tunduk SE operational team.
regulatory_hurdles: Digital Code AI auditability provisions are still being detailed by KG-AI-SECONDARY-REG-WORKING-GROUP. Vendor must follow the secondary regulation drafting closely to avoid building against an outdated specification. Mitigation: bid as part of the same vendor stack participating in Digital Code secondary regulation drafting (linked initiative KG-INI-008).

Local Kyrgyz integrators (HTP residents) lack API-gateway and observability depth. Open positioning if vendor can field Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual + modern cloud-native API stack + AI inference fabric simultaneously — a triple Cybernetica cannot match.

short_name: KG eHealth EHR & AI Diagnostic Platform
one_liner: Deliver electronic health record and AI diagnostic suite for the Ministry of Health under live RFP KG-T-2026-006 ($4.03M), replicating Estonia e-Health and Kazakhstan Damumed precedents.
problem_statement: KG-MINHEALTH lacks national EHR; existing data is fragmented across hospital systems. Live tender KG-T-2026-006 ($4.03M, digital health: EHR + AI diagnostic support) is open. Constitutional commitment to digital governance (KG-UP-2024-090-CONCEPT) and Digital Code (KG-LAW-2025-178) mandate health-data interoperability via Tunduk. AKDN-KG-DIGITAL-SCHOOLS2030 ($15M, AKDN) and UNICEF-KG-DIGITAL-EARLY ($1.5M) provide co-financing pathway for child and rural health. Estonia E-Health (case-est-ehealth), Kazakhstan Damumed (case-kz-damumed), and Bangladesh a2i Telemedicine (case-bd-a2i-health) are precedent cases. KG mountain geography (>90% mountainous, scattered population) makes telemedicine + AI triage especially high-value.
solution_concept: Three-layer platform: (1) National EHR core with Tunduk-bound identity (KGz citizen ID), patient data store, and clinician-facing UX in Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual; (2) AI diagnostic suite — radiology image triage (chest X-ray TB screening priority, given KG TB burden), retinal screening for diabetic retinopathy, ECG arrhythmia detection — running as inference services on Tunduk inference fabric (linked to KG-INI-003); (3) Telemedicine triage for mountain communities (linked to KG-INI-006), AKDN co-financed, with offline-capable mobile app for ayil ambulatories. Architectural anchor: Estonia e-terviseportaal (case-est-ehealth) + Damumed clinical decision support (case-kz-damumed) + a2i community-clinic delivery model (case-bd-a2i-health). Adapted for KG's centralized procurement, Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual UX, Tunduk integration, and mountain telemedicine field constraints.
what_preserved: Estonia e-Health architecture: patient record data store, X-Road-bound consent, clinician-facing portal — proven in production for 1.3M citizens since 2008.
what_adapted: Tunduk integration (rather than X-Road), Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual UX, AI diagnostic suite (Estonia e-Health is foundational EHR not AI-heavy), telemedicine offline mountain delivery (AKDN-funded use case absent in Estonia), Damumed-style clinical decision support imported on top.
regulatory_hurdles: Personal information law KG-LAW-2008-058 + Digital Code data localization for sensitive personal data (health). Mitigation: deploy on Tunduk-aligned data residency, no cross-border PHI flow without explicit consent receipt.

InterSystems and Allscripts (international EHR vendors) have presence via WB but expensive and not Russian-Kyrgyz native. Estonia e-Health team via eGA twinning (kg-tonis-mae) advisory. Local KG integrators lack AI diagnostic depth. Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual + AI diagnostic + AKDN telemedicine integration is the differentiator package.

Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual clinician UX with named clinician users at Bishkek Republican Hospital

short_name: KG Identity & Social Protection AI Registry (WB P155198)
one_liner: Deliver AI-augmented identity and social protection registry for Ministry of Labor & Social Protection under World Bank Project P155198 ($20M), replicating Kazakhstan e-Otinish and India e-Shram.
problem_statement: WB-KG-IDENTITY-P155198 ($20M) is the active World Bank Identity and Targeting for Social Protection Project. Ministry of Labor and Social Protection (KG-MINLABOR / kg-minsoc-head) is implementing partner. Existing Kyrgyz social registry has data quality gaps and lacks AI-assisted targeting. KG-LAW-2008-058 (personal information) and Digital Code provide regulatory frame. case-kz-smart-social Kazakhstan e-Otinish, case-in-e-shram India e-Shram informal labor registry, and case-pl-mobywatel Poland mObywatel (Soviet-bloc evolution reference) are precedents. The system is a foundation for cash-transfer targeting, child protection, labor market matching, and post-pandemic resilience.
solution_concept: Three-layer AI registry: (1) data-quality AI engine — entity resolution, deduplication, and gap detection across existing social registry, civil registry (KG-GRS), tax (KG-GNS), and Tunduk identity records, with named uncertainty for each record; (2) targeting AI — proxy means testing model for cash-transfer eligibility, with explainable scores and human-review workflow; (3) caseworker assistant — Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual conversational interface for social workers in 7 oblast offices to query the registry, draft case notes, and route applications. Architectural anchor: Kazakhstan e-Otinish social registry + India e-Shram unorganized worker pattern. Adapted for KG centralized social fund administration, Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual UX, Tunduk-bound identity, and AKDN/SDC rural inclusion overlap.
what_preserved: Kazakhstan e-Otinish architecture: registry, targeting, caseworker UX.
what_adapted: KG centralized social fund (KG-SOCIAL-FUND), Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual UX, Tunduk identity binding, AKDN rural inclusion overlap, integration with WB P155198 PIU procurement modality.
regulatory_hurdles: Personal data law and social-protection confidentiality. Mitigation: Tunduk-aligned residency, explicit consent receipts, role-based access for caseworkers.
competitive_landscape: Existing Phase 1 vendor relationships are on data digitalization, not AI augmentation. Kazakhstan e-Otinish vendor present regionally. International social registry vendors (DSDIA, GovStack) lack Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual depth. Open positioning for Russian-Kyrgyz bilingual + AI registry + AKDN rural integration.
mandatory_local_partner: Social Fund of KG (KG-SOCIAL-FUND) + HTP IT integrator + AKDN rural partnership for outreach.
